summary: The service started this run, not an instruction, because a baseline width-200 loop (job 164687, f* 0.65) ended. There were no Asked items, so there is nothing to answer as asked, and no claims were proposed or changed. The run read the six width-200 loops that have ended so far and wrote an interim evidence file. I re-derived every per-step number from the mirrored summary.json files, and all of them match, including all fifty recorded SHA-256 checksums. The f* 0.65 loop completed forty-three steps, its floor was Gamma 2.4 (overlap at 2.35) and its ceiling 3.9 (overlap at 3.95). Its median cost was 0.908 CPU-hours per 25-cycle step. The f* 0.84, 0.33, 0.30 and 0.27 loops broke with a sphere overlap at Gamma 3.0 after zero or one cycle. The nudge loop at f* 0.27 hit its 4 CPU-hour first-step cap after 49 of 50 cycles. In every ended loop, no step gained energy, failed the audit or had a slow episode. The width-100 comparison values (only f* 0.27 failed at the start there; f* 0.65 reached 2.25 and 4.1) match evidence/E0073-results.json. Two statements need correcting. (1) The run says three times that the nudge caps were 'the ones Chris kept on Nov 22', in the summary, the L0018 progress.md ('caps kept, Nov 22') and PROGRAM.md. No such reply exists. The Nov 22 instruction has no L0018 section and does not mention CPU caps; its only 'keep' is 'keep the capture threshold at 1e-4', which is in L0019's section and is about a different thing. What actually happened is that the Nov 21 question on the E0075 caps went unanswered, so its default (let the loops run and stop) applied. Leaving the loop stopped is reasonable, but the reason should not be put in Chris's mouth. (2) The L0018 line state ends 'Cost per step at width 200 is about 5.5 times width 100, as the cost holds measured', and the experiment takeaway says the cost 'agrees with' E0070's 4.7 to 5.6. The 5.52 divides the width-200 median of 25-cycle steps (0.908) by the width-100 mean over all fifty-five steps, which includes its 50-cycle first step and its two failed steps (9.05 / 55 = 0.165). Built the same way on both sides (total CPU over all steps), the ratio is 6.2. Using the width-200 mean of 25-cycle steps (0.969) instead, it is 5.9. Both are above E0070's range. The width-100 loop also covered a wider and costlier Gamma range (its steps get dearer toward the floor), so even 6.2 is not like-for-like. The evidence file's own note calls the ratio 'rough', but the line state drops that caveat and states agreement. 'About five to six times, not measured like-for-like' is what the evidence supports. One observation the run did not draw out bears on its proposed seed rerun. The f* 0.30 and 0.27 baseline loops used 1.66 and 3.15 CPU-hours without completing more than one cycle. The f* 0.65 loop's whole 50-cycle first step cost 1.67 CPU-hours. So at low f* the half-push start was slow and dense before it overlapped. That points at the start state, not only at 'four times as many particles', so the run was right to call the size effect unmeasured. program check fails only because of my own scratch folder sequel-data/checker/, which CHECKER.md tells me to use and program check flags as unrecorded data. I deleted it before committing, and program check passes afterwards. The four approvals in the last day (Nov 23 15:06, 15:47, 15:49 and Nov 24 03:19) are human-file approvals that program check accepts; whether they were Chris's is for Chris to confirm. sequel-data is 368 megabytes, against a 15 gigabyte ceiling. Free disk is 92 gigabytes, above the 40 gigabyte floor. tmp/ is empty, and the run wrote nothing outside the two allowed folders. The run's whole job was to examine ended loops, so no time went to unasked work. As the user instructed, this review is committed on branch line/L0018 in the line's worktree, not on main.

run_conditions.assessment: This was a short service run. The job record says the job ended at 04:25:16, the run started at 04:26, and its commit is at 04:30:35. It used no local CPU and ran no simulations: it only read fetched outputs, and zero CPU-hours is right. Twenty-four width-200 loops are still running on Hatteras, and none was restarted, cancelled or started. The host is the Linux container, so pmset and uptime are unavailable and sleep could not be checked, which the summary says. Free disk was 92 gigabytes, as recorded. The weekly CPU budget is 493 of 10000 hours (5 percent), which matches program check. The machine did not limit the science.
discrepancies: The summary's 'ended' time is 04:33:00, but the run's commit is 04:30:35 and this checker started at 04:31:32. The end time was written ahead of time, not measured.
active.jsonl is empty, though 24 width-200 jobs are running. That is consistent with the cluster rule (program jobs tracks Hatteras jobs, and active.jsonl is for local jobs), so this is not a fault.
